## How they got there
Paris Saint-Germain won the title by beating Inter 5-0 in the final, a result achieved while ranking eighth among the season's knockout teams. Their profile was defined by high offensive output, with 65.5 attacks per game better than 97% of that season's group/league-phase teams and 13.2 shots per game also better than 97%. They further distinguished themselves through volume in possession, recording 656 passes per game which placed them ahead of 94% of their peers in the league phase.

## Would the model have picked them?
Although the club's probability of reaching the final stood at 10.1%, exceeding the base rate of 8.3%, the model ranked them eighth and therefore did not pick them, as it only selects teams in its top two. The system's expectation was nearest to the quarter-finals stage, with an expected value of 0.82 on a scale where zero represents elimination before that round. This indicates that despite beating the base rate probability, the team's overall statistical profile did not meet the model's threshold for selection given the strict requirement for top-two ranking among knockout participants.

## Weak spots
The final two stats in the list, long passes at 9.1% and shot conversion at 13.2%, represent areas where the team beat fewer than half of the teams compared to their league-phase peers. While the model marked down long passes with a negative contribution, Paris Saint-Germain still ranked better than 17% of that season's group/league-phase teams on this metric. Similarly, although shot conversion received a negative signal from the model, the team performed better than 26% of their league-phase counterparts in converting shots into goals.

messages.content: You are a football performance analyst writing for a curious, data-literate reader. Use ONLY the facts provided. Quote every number exactly as it appears in the facts, with the same rounding. Do not introduce players, managers, matches, events, analyses or numbers that are not in the facts. 'Better than this %' figures say how many teams the club beat on a stat, so higher is always better, including for stats marked '(lower is better)', where beating a team means having the lower value. Write them as 'better than X% of teams', never as 'top X%'. SHAP contributions are measured in knockout stages: a positive contribution means the stat pushed the model's expected stage up by that fraction of a round, a negative one pushed it down. A SHAP contribution is the model's view, not a measure of how good the team was at the stat: a team can rank high on a stat the model marked down, so never call a stat a strength or a weakness because of its SHAP sign. Everything here is a statistical association, not a cause: never say a stat or a team's profile drove, powered, propelled, carried, helped, hindered or prevented a result, and do not explain why a stat got its contribution. Write plain markdown without tables.
